text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 1% today and has climbed 7.3% over the past two weeks, driven largely by escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East that has pushed crude oil prices higher and kept refineries running at 98% capacity. Iran's strikes on Kuwait and U.S. allies, combined with reports of mines near the Hormuz Strait—a critical passage for global oil shipments—have created supply uncertainty that lifts the value of refined products like gasoline and diesel, boosting refiner margins.

The company is also benefiting from tighter fuel supplies: US oil storage sits at 711 million barrels (relatively low) while gasoline inventory is just over 205 million barrels, meaning refiners can sell what they produce at stronger prices. With refineries running flat-out and Middle East tensions keeping the market on edge, the refining business has become more profitable.
